First, we find the roots of the characteristic polynomial:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+64 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2} & =-64 \\ \lambda  & =\pm 8\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =P\operatorname{cos}⁡8x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡8x\end{aligned}
$$

We find the constants $P$ and $Q$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(\pi )=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}P=1.\end{aligned}
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(\pi )=4,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
{y}^{′}=-8P\operatorname{sin}⁡8x+8Q\operatorname{cos}⁡8x.
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(\pi )=4$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}8Q=4\,⟹\,Q=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=\operatorname{cos}⁡8x+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡8x.
$$
